newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent futures hold firm in rangebound market.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent futures hold firm in rangebound market.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil continued to hold firm around the $22.30 a barrel area at midday on Tuesday supported by technicals in rangebound trading, dealers said.
March Brent was up 25 cents at $22.30 at 1320 GMT, off an intra-day high of $22.39, but well above Monday's $22.05 close.
Brokers said there was some technical support from the morning's bounce but no fundamental supporting factors and said they expected to see the market turn to the downside again.
"I think we'll probably see a bit more to the downside of the market, but apart from that we're just holding at the moment," one broker said.
MeesPiersen Derivatives Ltd said in a daily market report they expected Brent to range-trade between $22.20 and $22.55 a barrel, cutting any shorts on a break above that level.
February gas oil was up $2 at $201.75 a tonne, still holding shy of breaching the psychological $200 barrier again after hovering just below it for most of Monday.
Some dealers saw gas oil supported by possible heating oil boosts due to colder weather forecast over the next few days.
Independent weather forecaster Weather Services Corp saw below average temperatures over the next week in the key heating oil market of the U.S. northeast.
This was likely to result in "above normal heating demand for the next week to 10 days."
Weekly stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) are due to be released after the market closes on Tuesday.

Leslie Nicholas of GNI Research said in his daily report this data was likely to be the main focus for the week. "Heating oil needs a stock fall to support it, especially with the weather in Europe moderate in many of the main demand centres," he said.
